deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is not by Riemann. It is the closing page of a letter from R. Dedekind to H. Weber, dated Braunschweig, 2 April 1876. It concerns the editing of Riemann's 'Fragmente über die Grenzfälle der elliptischen Modulfunctionen' for Riemann's Werke (1876), fragment XXVIII. On the previous page Dedekind compared Riemann's limit formulas with his own, which he derived from the transformation of log eta(omega).

Notation from the previous page: q = e^{pi i omega}, q0 = e^{pi i omega0} with omega0 = M/N in lowest terms, A = pi i/(24 N^2 (omega - omega0)), B = (1/2) log((omega - omega0)/i) + (1/2) log N. Dedekind found that Riemann's imaginary parts need only tiny corrections. Riemann's real parts, however, differ from the correct values by constants such as log(2N/pi), (1/N) log(...) and 2 log 2.

(a) Editorial proposal. Make the tiny corrections in the imaginary parts. Leave the real parts as Riemann wrote them, and add a warning in the commentary.

(b) Diagnosis of Riemann's term (1/n) log((1+q^n)/(1-q^n)). As q -> 1, (1-q)/(1-q^n) -> 1/n. Dedekind conjectures that Riemann, in haste, wrote (1/n) log(...) where log(1/n) was meant. (Reading: limit of log((1-q)/(1-q^n)) = log(1/n); the gloss is mine.)

(c) The only place showing how Riemann treated real parts (6th piece, t running over odd numbers):
- log(2K/pi) = 4 sum_{t odd} (1/t) q^t/(1+q^t).
- Equivalently, 2K/pi = theta3(q)^2.
- Subtract log((q0+q)/(q0-q)) = 2 sum_{t odd} (q/q0)^t / t. This holds because log((1+x)/(1-x)) = 2 sum_{t odd} x^t/t with x = q/q0.
- Result: log(2K/pi) = log((q0+q)/(q0-q)) + 4 sum_{t odd} (1/t) ( q^t/(1+q^t) - (1/2)(q/q0)^t ).

(d) Real part of the remainder. Put q = r q0 with |q0| = 1 and 0 < r < 1, so that conj(q0^t) = q0^{-t}.
- Using Re z = (z + conj z)/2, the t-th term gives (r^t/2) [ q0^t/(1+r^t q0^t) + q0^{-t}/(1+r^t q0^{-t}) - 1 ].
- Hence Re(second sum) = 2 sum (r^t/t) ( q0^t/(1+r^t q0^t) + q0^{-t}/(1+r^t q0^{-t}) - 1 ).

(e) Behaviour at r = 1.
- At r = 1 the bracket is q0^t/(1+q0^t) + 1/(1+q0^t) - 1 = 0, termwise (provided q0^t ≠ -1).
- Dedekind suspects this led Riemann to treat the series as infinitesimal as r -> 1.
- Dedekind holds, from his eta formulas, that the series is discontinuous at r = 1 and tends to log(pi/(2n)) (n = N), not 0. In modern terms the convergence is non-uniform, and termwise passage to the limit is illegitimate.
- This matches the previous page: Riemann's real part of log(2K/pi) is -2B + log(2N/pi), whereas the correct value is -2B.

(f) Further diagnosis.
- Separating out the terms whose index is divisible by n yields Riemann's (1/n) log((1+q^n)/(1-q^n)).
- These are the terms where q0^t can equal -1 and the bracket blows up.
- This does not exhaust everything that becomes infinite, or finite and non-zero.
- Since Dedekind cannot find a proper form for the correction, he keeps the (in his view wrong) real parts, with a warning, excused by the fragmentary character of the work.

(g) Non-mathematical business.
- He asks Weber to keep the letter-sheets on his 'Ideal-Theorie' and encloses a continuation; the next sheet will begin the actual multiplication of ideals.
- Proof sheet 28 has arrived; he corrected (m,n) to 2(m,n) throughout.
- For the inaccuracies above, his inserted words 'in den reellen Theilen' should suffice.
- He corrected the second revise of sheet 27 only from the 'Addit.' onward; a formula at the top of the last page needs changing in one of the ways indicated below (N.B.).
- Greetings to Weber, Frau Gemahlin, Ida and Rudi.
errors: No error in Dedekind's computations. The series identity, the real-part formula and the vanishing of the bracket at r=1 all check.

Caveat implicit in the text: the bracket vanishes at r=1 only for q0^t ≠ -1. For t with M t/N an odd integer the term is singular. Dedekind notes that separating these terms (giving Riemann's (1/n) log((1+q^n)/(1-q^n))) still does not account for the full finite limit.

Dedekind's claim that the remaining real series tends to log(pi/(2n)) rather than 0 is correct, at least in the checkable case N=1, q0=1. There, 2 log theta3(e^{-eps}) ~ log(pi/eps) and log((1+q)/(1-q)) ~ log(2/eps), so the difference tends to log(pi/2). Riemann's tacit termwise limit is thus the error (non-uniform convergence).
Dedekind's 'haste' explanation, (1/n) log versus log(1/n), is only a conjecture about the origin of Riemann's slip.

results.what: log(2K/pi) = 2 log theta3(q) = 4 sum_{t odd} q^t/(t(1+q^t))
results.modern_name: Lambert-type series for log theta3 / log(2K/pi) (Jacobi)

results.what: Riemann's limiting real parts in the 'Grenzfälle' fragments are wrong by constants (log(2N/pi), 2 log 2), due to interchanging the limit r->1 with an infinite sum whose terms vanish individually
results.modern_name: Non-uniform convergence at the boundary; asymptotics of theta/eta at rational cusps via the modular transformation
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind, Erläuterungen zu den Riemann'schen Fragmenten über die Grenzfälle der elliptischen Modulfunctionen (Riemann's Werke 1876)

results.what: Use of the transformation of log eta(omega) near omega0 = M/N to get correct boundary behaviour (constants A, B)
results.modern_name: Dedekind eta transformation formula / Dedekind sums

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a Dedekind-to-Weber letter of 1876 about editing Riemann's fragment XXVIII; it contains no new Riemann mathematics. Dedekind's critique of Riemann's real parts and his eta-based corrections are known from his published 'Erläuterungen' and the Dedekind–Weber editorial correspondence. The most notable detail is the explicit diagnosis of non-uniform convergence and the decision to leave Riemann's real parts uncorrected with a warning.

checkable.asserts: 2 log theta3(q) = 4 sum_{t odd} q^t/(t(1+q^t)), i.e. log(2K/pi), up to O(q^25)

checkable.asserts: log((1+x)/(1-x)) = 2 sum_{t odd} x^t/t, so 4 sum (1/t)(1/2)(q/q0)^t = log((q0+q)/(q0-q))

At r=1 the bracket vanishes identically (w = q0^t ≠ -1)
Case N=1, q0=1: continuum limit of 2 sum_{t odd} (r^t/t)(1-r^t)/(1+r^t) as r->1 equals log(pi/2) ≠ 0, confirming Dedekind's claim of a jump to log(pi/(2n))
(1-q)/(1-q^n) -> 1/n as q->1 (here n=5), the basis of Dedekind's conjecture about Riemann's slip

transcription_corrections: Author and date: the page is a letter of R. Dedekind (Braunschweig, 2 April 1876), presumably to H. Weber, not a Riemann manuscript.
'weil (1-q)/(1-q^n) = 1/n ist': this is meant for q=1 (limit); the image has a small mark or superscript after q in the numerator.
The question marks after 'gekommen' and 'verwechselt' carry small superscript footnote marks (1, 2) in the image.
'(im 6ten Stück) (ungerade Zahlen)': the summation index t runs over odd numbers only.
'der oben angeregten[?] Unrichtigkeiten' is uncertain in the image; possibly 'oben angezeigten'.
In the final formula the exponents are q0^{t} and q0^{-t}, as transcribed; the image confirms this.
